item.text: {"search_note":"I did not find a 2024 source that directly measured dignity or equal opportunity outcomes across groups in a systematic way. The best positive evidence is programmatic and design-level, not proof of broad lived equality. The strongest negative evidence is rights- and repression-based, not a dedicated national equality audit.","evidence":[{"title":"DR Congo president appoints country's first female prime minister","publisher":"Reuters","date":"2024-04-01","url":"https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/dr-congo-president-appoints-countrys-first-female-prime-minister-2024-04-01/","summary":"Tshisekedi appointed Judith Suminwa, DRC’s first female prime minister. That is a real inclusion signal and directly supports equal-opportunity rather than purely aggregate-welfare governance.","question_ids":["6B.8"]},{"title":"Biographie de la Première Ministre","publisher":"Primature","date":"2024","url":"https://www.primature.gouv.cd/biographie-de-la-premiere-ministre/","summary":"Suminwa’s official biography stresses applied economics, banking, UN/PNUD experience, and development-planning work. That supports a competence-plus-inclusion reading rather than a pure loyalty appointment.","question_ids":["6B.8"]},{"title":"DR Congo: Expanding and Equipping Primary School Classrooms for Better Learning Outcomes","publisher":"World Bank","date":"2024-02-28","url":"https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/02/28/democratic-republic-congo-afe-expanding-and-equipping-primary-school-classrooms-for-better-learning-outcomes","summary":"The education project explicitly aimed at students with disabilities, girls’ access, merit-based teacher recruitment, and decentralized planning. This is the clearest evidence I found for protecting equal opportunity through service design, not just aggregate output.","question_ids":["6B.8","6B.2","6B.5"]},{"title":"UNICEF cash-transfer gender/social protection report","publisher":"UNICEF Innocenti","date":"2024-02","url":"https://www.unicef.org/innocenti/reports/grassp-democratic-republic-congo","summary":"A cash-transfer program in Kinshasa-area neighborhoods targeted the most vulnerable households and also trained local associations on women’s leadership, women’s rights, and gender-based violence. That is positive evidence for dignity and subgroup-sensitive support.","question_ids":["6B.8","6B.6"]},{"title":"UNICEF scales up efforts to protect children from mpox outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo","publisher":"UNICEF","date":"2024-09-12","url":"https://www.unicef.org/press-releases/unicef-scales-efforts-protect-children-mpox-outbreak-democratic-republic-congo","summary":"UNICEF’s response plan prioritized children under 15 in 12 provinces and described free treatment for a child. That is a concrete dignity/equal-protection signal for a vulnerable group during a crisis.","question_ids":["6B.8","6B.6"]},{"title":"DR Congo: President Tshisekedi must use second term to tackle human rights crisis","publisher":"Amnesty International","date":"2024-06-24","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/drc-president-tshisekedi-must-use-second-term-to-tackle-human-rights-crisis/","summary":"Amnesty said Tshisekedi had made numerous human-rights pledges but little progress, and that socioeconomic injustice and shrinking civic space persisted. This is strong negative evidence against dignity-centered rule.","question_ids":["6B.8"]},{"title":"DRC President Felix Tshisekedi must be held accountable for human rights violations","publisher":"Amnesty International","date":"2024-09-30","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/drc-president-felix-tshisekedi-must-be-held-accountable-for-human-rights-violations/","summary":"Amnesty said the state of siege militarized daily life and that the government failed to protect civilians and address deep-rooted socioeconomic injustices. That cuts directly against a dignity-first reading.","question_ids":["6B.8","6B.7"]},{"title":"DR Congo: Second term should focus rights","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024-03-06","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/03/06/dr-congo-second-term-should-focus-rights","summary":"HRW said Tshisekedi’s first term ended with repression, arbitrary arrests, and mistrust in democratic institutions, and urged human-rights-centered governance. This is strong evidence that dignity and equal treatment were not being reliably protected.","question_ids":["6B.8"]},{"title":"World Report 2024: Democratic Republic of Congo","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024","url":"https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/democratic-republic-congo","summary":"HRW reported ongoing repression against journalists, activists, critics, and opposition members, plus police violence against peaceful protest. That is direct counterevidence to dignity and equal-citizenship protection.","question_ids":["6B.8","6B.7"]},{"title":"DR Congo: Reinstating executions shows a callous disregard for human rights","publisher":"Amnesty International","date":"2024-03-15","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/03/drc-reinstating-executions-shows-a-callous-disregard-for-human-rights/","summary":"Restoring executions was framed as a hardline response to violence, but Amnesty said it endangered people on death row and violated the right to life. That is strong negative evidence for dignity protection.","question_ids":["6B.8","6B.7"]},{"title":"Human Rights Agenda for the Democratic Republic of Congo","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024-03-06","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/03/06/human-rights-agenda-democratic-republic-congo","summary":"HRW noted that elections were marred by irregularities and violence, and that the new term should reverse rights backsliding. This supports the view that equal political dignity was not secure.","question_ids":["6B.8","4B.1"]}]}
